relevance_note: Letter describing two individuals with GFAP variants: "We describe 2 cases of genetically confirmed juvenile-onset AD".
method_note: Built by a short Python script from a manual reading of the paper (no tables in the paper). Labels 'Case 1' and 'Case 2' are the paper's section headings (also 'as seen in Case 1'); the figure legend calls them 'Patient 1'/'Patient 2', taken as the same people. The Markdown renders '>' as '>'; spans keep '>' verbatim, while variant values use '>' as printed in the article. Case 1's variant is printed only as 'heterozygous C>T nucleotide substitution in exon 4 at amino acid position 258' (no c. or p. notation), so cdna/protein fields are null; variant type not stated for either variant (the intro's general 'de novo heterozygous missense mutations' is about the disorder, not these patients, so not used for type, zygosity or inheritance). Case 2 zygosity and pathogenicity not stated ('a mutation'). No parental testing reported. is_proband left null: two unrelated cases, neither called proband. Publication year not printed in the document. Ages: Case 1 '7-year-old' at referral is the only age given and is recorded as age at last evaluation; Case 2 was 14 at presentation and had a later event 'Three years later' (no age written), so age at last evaluation is not reported. Case 2 'developmental delay' recorded observed because an MRI was done 'for investigation of developmental delay'. Case 2 'No motor symptoms ... at the time of presentation' (excluded) and later 'dense right hemiplegia' (observed) are at different times, not a contradiction; checklist limb weakness = observed from the later hemiplegia. Normal-as-a-whole statements not converted to specific exclusions: 'Neurological examination was unremarkable apart from...' and 'Extensive neuro-metabolic and neuro-inflammatory investigations ... yielded no significant abnormality'. Out of scope: the 3 previously reported juvenile AD cases and the 10 patients of the cited 2005 study (no individual-level detail). Discussion statement that Type II features (later onset, bulbar symptoms, atypical MRI) are 'illustrated in both cases' was not used to mark bulbar features.
